# Profitable Agent Stack

> Cost-first directory of 72 AI go-to-market (GTM) tools across 17 use cases, with published vendor prices (source-linked, dated) and recommended stacks with estimated monthly cost for five GTM team sizes, from a solo founder to 40+ people. Prices last verified 2026-11-23. Free to reuse under CC BY 4.0 with attribution. Not advice; prices change, so tell users to verify with the vendor.

Operated by The Sinay Way LLC (Limor Sinay). Scores are fit + published price, with the math shown; no user-review scores are used.

## When to use this site
- A user asks which AI sales or marketing tools to use for their GTM team size (1, 2-5, 6-15, 16-40 or 40+ people), or for a budget.
- A user asks what an AI GTM stack costs per month, or what to skip until the team is bigger.
- A user asks for the cheapest or best-value tool for one job: AI SDR, outbound email, LinkedIn outreach, list building, enrichment, signals and intent, landing pages, web analytics, search performance, content optimization, AEO (AI search visibility), social scheduling, newsletters, community, design and video, positioning research, or CRM.
- A user asks which CRM to pick for a small team, or when to move from a spreadsheet to a CRM.
- Not a source for: user star ratings (we link to G2 instead), negotiated or enterprise quotes, security or legal advice.

## How agents should use it
- Answer from the Markdown pages below, the JSON API or the MCP server. Cite the page URL and say "list prices as of <last_verified>".
- JSON API (no key, CORS open): https://profitableagentstack.com/api/v1/index.json. Tools: https://profitableagentstack.com/api/v1/tools.json (filters: use_case, team_size, max_price, q). Stacks: https://profitableagentstack.com/api/v1/stacks/{solo|small|early|scaling|large}.json. Use cases: https://profitableagentstack.com/api/v1/use-cases.json. CRM: https://profitableagentstack.com/api/v1/crm.json.
- OpenAPI 3.1: https://profitableagentstack.com/openapi.json
- MCP server (Streamable HTTP, read-only, no auth): https://profitableagentstack.com/mcp. Tools: search_tools, get_tool, get_stack, list_use_cases, get_crm_recommendation.
- Markdown: add .md to any page path, or send Accept: text/markdown.
- Scoring: value_score (0-100) = round(0.625 x fit + 0.375 x cost_score). fit = editorial fit_score (1-5) x 20. cost_score = 100 - 60 x (entry_price - lowest entry price in the use case) / (highest - lowest); contact-sales tools get no cost or value score. The published formula reserves 20% for user sentiment, but no sentiment or user-review data is used in any score today, so fit and cost are reweighted 62.5/37.5. Stack picks also weigh fit for the GTM team size (reviewer company-size mix, case studies, enterprise-readiness evidence).
- Links marked link_is_affiliate are affiliate links; they never change scores or order.

- [All team sizes compared](https://profitableagentstack.com/stages/index.md)
- [Solo founder (1 GTM person)](https://profitableagentstack.com/stages/solo-founder.md): about $41/mo + €19 Waalaxy
- [Small GTM team (2–5 GTM people)](https://profitableagentstack.com/stages/small-gtm-team.md): about $106/mo + €38 Waalaxy (2 users)

- [Scaling (16–40 GTM people)](https://profitableagentstack.com/stages/scaling.md): about $2,193/mo
- [Large / multi-team (40+ GTM people)](https://profitableagentstack.com/stages/large-multi-team.md): at least $7,587/mo

## Answers and guides
- [Quick answers: best stack by team size, cheapest tool per use case, CRM picks](https://profitableagentstack.com/answers.md)
- [Directory of all tools](https://profitableagentstack.com/directory.md)
- [New releases and price changes](https://profitableagentstack.com/new-releases.md)
- [When to add AEO (AI search visibility) vs classic SEO](https://profitableagentstack.com/articles/when-to-add-aeo.md): AEO tools track whether ChatGPT, Perplexity and Google's AI answers mention your brand. Classic search tools come first; add AEO when AI assistants already send you visits.
- [Why we size stacks by GTM team size, not funding stage](https://profitableagentstack.com/articles/stacks-by-gtm-team-size.md): Funding rounds say little about what tools you need. How many people do go-to-market says a lot.
- [When to skip intent data (and what to do first)](https://profitableagentstack.com/articles/when-to-skip-intent-data.md): Intent and signals tools help you prioritize. If you have nobody worth prioritizing yet, they are an expensive distraction.
- [One tool per job: how to stop paying twice](https://profitableagentstack.com/articles/one-tool-per-job.md): Most GTM stacks pay for the same job two or three times. Here is how we pick one tool per job and explain each pick.
- [How we score AI GTM tools (and why cost counts)](https://profitableagentstack.com/articles/how-we-score.md): The value score in plain words: what goes in, what does not, and why money never changes rank.

# Full text (generated 2026-11-23)

## Scoring methodology
value_score (0-100) = round(0.625 x fit + 0.375 x cost_score). fit = editorial fit_score (1-5) x 20. cost_score = 100 - 60 x (entry_price - lowest entry price in the use case) / (highest - lowest); contact-sales tools get no cost or value score. The published formula reserves 20% for user sentiment, but no sentiment or user-review data is used in any score today, so fit and cost are reweighted 62.5/37.5. Stack picks also weigh fit for the GTM team size (reviewer company-size mix, case studies, enterprise-readiness evidence).

## All tools (ranked by value score)

### Apollo
- Use case: List building & lead data (list-building)
- Fits GTM team sizes: Solo founder (1 GTM person), Small GTM team (2–5 GTM people), Early scaling (6–15 GTM people), Scaling (16–40 GTM people), Large / multi-team (40+ GTM people)
- Price: Free Starter plan (no time limit; Apollo's FAQ calls it for 'exploring or very light usage'); Basic $49, Professional $79, Organization $119 per seat/mo billed annually (Organization: 3-seat minimum, SSO listed in plan table); Custom plan for SSO, advanced security and custom volumes via sales (entry USD 0/mo)
- Last verified: 2026-11-16
- Pricing source: https://www.apollo.io/pricing
- Scores: fit 5/5 (editorial), cost 100, value 100 (best value in its use case)
- In our recommended stacks: Solo founder, Small GTM team, Early scaling, Scaling, Large / multi-team
- Page: https://profitableagentstack.com/use-cases/list-building#apollo

# Solo founder: AI GTM stack for 1 GTM person, about $41/mo

About $41/mo + €19 Waalaxy for our recommended stack, estimated from published list prices as of 2026-11-02 to 2026-11-23 (per tool). Assumptions: 1 GTM person, 1 LinkedIn account, light volume. Hunter's free plan (50 credits/mo) caps how many new emails you can find; move up when you outgrow it. Monthly billing, entry tiers; Carrd is priced yearly ÷ 12. Actual cost depends on your usage, billing period, taxes and add-ons.

## Who this is for

One person doing all of go-to-market: you are the founder, the seller and the marketer. Your goal is the first repeatable customers, not a machine.

## Recommended stack (estimate)

One tool per job, no paid overlap. Each pick weighs two things: its value score and whether it fits a team of this size, judged from reviews by companies of similar size and from enterprise-readiness evidence. The value score is a category-wide number based on each tool's lowest published price (often a free plan), so a tool can be "best in category" and still not be the pick at this size. "Best in category" means the highest value score (ties included) among all tools we list for that use case.

- **Warm network & referrals.** Spreadsheet or notes app you already own. Message everyone you know who fits your ICP first; no tool is needed to do this.
- **ICP & positioning.** Customer conversations plus a one-page doc. We list no paid tool for this job: talk to buyers first.

| Use case | Best-value pick | Tier / assumption | Est. $/mo | Why this pick |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Sales stack** | | | | |
| List building & lead data | **[Apollo](https://www.apollo.io/)** value 100 · best in category | Free Starter plan | $0 | Highest value score for list building (free, fit 5/5). Exa is a free alternative if you prefer search-style prospecting. Free-plan limits change, so check them. |
| Enrichment & verification | **[Hunter](https://hunter.io/)** value 88 | Free plan (50 credits) | $0 | Free email finding and verification is enough for light hand-built lists. |
| Outbound email / sequencing | **[Smartlead](https://smartlead.ai?via=limor) affiliate** value 88 | Base, 1 workspace | $39 | Lowest published entry price for outbound email in our list. Instantly scores higher on value (94 vs 88) but costs $8 more; revisit at 2–5 people. |
| LinkedIn outreach | **[Waalaxy](https://waal.ink/N47esf) affiliate** value 88 · best in category | 1 user × €19 (EUR, not converted) | $0 | Cheapest listed LinkedIn tool and the best value score in its category. Per user, billed in euros. |
| **Marketing stack** | | | | |
| Landing pages & websites | **[Carrd](https://carrd.com/)** value 88 | Pro Standard, $19/yr ÷ 12 | $1.58 | Cheapest custom-domain landing page in our list; $19/yr is the yearly price on its Pro page. |
| Newsletters | **[beehiiv](https://www.beehiiv.com?via=limor-sinay) affiliate** value 100 · best in category | Free plan | $0 | Highest value score; free until you monetize. Kit is the free alternative (free up to 10,000 subscribers). |
| Web analytics | **[Google Analytics](https://marketingplatform.google.com/about/analytics/)** value 88 · best in category | Free | $0 | Free and good enough for basic traffic and source tracking at this size. |

## CRM for this team size (separate from the stack)

For 1 GTM person: **[HubSpot Sales Hub](https://www.hubspot.com/products/crm)**, Google Sheet first, then HubSpot Free CRM (up to 2 users) when a signal below appears, about **$0**. Runner-up: **[Attio](https://attio.com/)**, Free plan (up to 3 users), about $0. Not included in the stack total above.

|  | CRM | Tier / assumption | Est. cost |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Pick | **[HubSpot Sales Hub](https://www.hubspot.com/products/crm)** | Google Sheet first, then HubSpot Free CRM (up to 2 users) when a signal below appears | $0 |
| Runner-up | **[Attio](https://attio.com/)** | Free plan (up to 3 users) | $0 |

HubSpot Sales Hub has the largest small-business reviewer base among the CRMs we checked (60.5% of its G2 reviewers are small businesses) and native integrations with Apollo, Hunter, Smartlead and Waalaxy. Attio suits founders who want a flexible data model.

Also worth a look: Zoho CRM Free (3 users), Bigin by Zoho Free (1 user) and Close Solo ($9/mo billed annually, built-in calling) also fit here.

### Spreadsheet or CRM?

A sheet is usually enough while you are the only person selling, live deals stay under about 20 and most come from your network. Move to a free CRM the week you turn on a sequencer, or once a follow-up slips.

Signals that it is time for a CRM (our rules of thumb, not benchmarks):

- **A second person works the pipeline.** A cofounder, first seller, contractor SDR or agency. Shared sheets struggle with ownership, duplicates and overwritten notes.
- **More than about 20–30 live deals or conversations at once.** Or a follow-up has slipped more than once.
- **You copy sequencer replies into the sheet by hand.** More than about 30 minutes a week. Most CRMs here receive replies from Instantly, Smartlead or lemlist directly.
- **Email and LinkedIn reach the same people.** One record per person stops you double-touching prospects.
- **Investor or board pipeline reporting takes more than about an hour a month.** Stage history and pipeline reports are built into every CRM listed, including free plans (depth varies).
- **Inbound leads arrive or your first sales hire starts.** Forms, routing and activity history make the handoff work.

Starter sheet columns: Company, Contact, Email, LinkedIn URL, Source, Stage, Next step, Next-step date, Deal value, Last touch, Notes. Every CRM listed imports a CSV, so nothing is lost when you switch. List prices as of 2026-11-10 from vendor pricing pages; verify with the vendor. Seat counts follow this page's assumptions. [All CRMs we list](https://profitableagentstack.com/use-cases/crm).

## Use cases that matter at this size

- List building & lead data
- Enrichment & verification
- Outbound email / sequencing
- LinkedIn outreach
- Landing pages & websites
- Newsletters
- Web analytics

## Skip for now

- **Signals & intent data (RB2B, PostHog, Common Room).** Paid intent and visitor-identification tools tell you who to talk to. Until hand-built outbound gets replies, you have nobody to prioritize.
- **AI SDR / agentic SDR.** These are contact-sales products. An agent cannot fix messaging that does not work by hand yet.
- **Social scheduling, search and content tools, design/video, community.** Useful later; none of them is needed to get the first customers. Free Search Console is worth setting up when you publish.
- **AEO (AI search visibility) tools.** No AI-search demand to measure yet, and warm leads and outbound come first. Revisit when content gets traffic.

## Who this is for

Two to five people share go-to-market. Warm intros and hand outbound already produce some meetings, and you now want a repeatable sequence plus a little content.

## Recommended stack (estimate)

One tool per job, no paid overlap. Each pick weighs two things: its value score and whether it fits a team of this size, judged from reviews by companies of similar size and from enterprise-readiness evidence. - **Warm network & referrals.** Still your best channel. Keep it in a shared spreadsheet or your CRM.
- **ICP & positioning.** Revisit with real call notes; no paid tool listed for this job.

### Spreadsheet or CRM?

A shared sheet can work for a short while, but at 2–5 a second person usually already works the pipeline, which is the clearest signal to add a CRM.

- **Investor or board pipeline reporting takes more than about an hour a month.** Stage history and pipeline reports are built into every CRM listed, including free plans (depth varies).
- **Inbound leads arrive or your first sales hire starts.** Forms, routing and activity history make the handoff work.

- Enrichment & verification
- Outbound email / sequencing

- Web analytics

## Skip for now

- **Paid signals & intent data.** Use at most the free RB2B plan, and only once outbound is booking meetings.
- **AI SDR / agentic SDR.** Contact-sales pricing and little to feed it yet.
- **Content optimization (Surfer), video, community.** Use Search Console and publish first; add paid content tools once content is a weekly habit.
- **AEO (AI search visibility) tools.** Skip until AI assistants send you visits you can see in analytics; warm leads and outbound still produce more pipeline than AI-search visibility.

## Who this is for

Sixteen to forty people in go-to-market, several managers, and RevOps starting to own reports, permissions and data hygiene.

## Recommended stack (estimate)

One tool per job, no paid overlap. Each pick weighs two things: its value score and whether it fits a team of this size, judged from reviews by companies of similar size and from enterprise-readiness evidence. The value score is a category-wide number based on each tool's lowest published price (often a free plan), so a tool can be "best in category" and still not be the pick at this size. "Best in category" means the highest value score (ties included) among all tools we list for that use case.

- **Warm network & referrals.** Sourced and tracked in the CRM, not a tool in this stack.
- **ICP & positioning.** Owned by product marketing; no paid tool listed.

Step up to Clay Growth ($495/mo monthly list) when RevOps needs CRM auto-sync, phone numbers and signals; the Large stack uses Clay. |

## CRM for this team size (separate from the stack)

For 16–40 GTM people: **[HubSpot Sales Hub](https://www.hubspot.com/products/crm)**, Professional, 25 seats × $90 billed annually, plus $1,500 one-time onboarding, about **$2,250/mo + $1,500 one-time**. Runner-up: **[Salesforce Sales Cloud](https://www.salesforce.com/sales/)**, Pro Suite, 25 seats × $100 (billed annually, contract), about $2,500/mo. Not included in the stack total above.

| Runner-up | **[Salesforce Sales Cloud](https://www.salesforce.com/sales/)** | Pro Suite, 25 seats × $100 (billed annually, contract) | $2,500/mo |

Professional adds forecasting and advanced automation. Salesforce has the largest mid-market and enterprise reviewer base in the category (45.7% mid-market, 33.7% enterprise of its G2 reviewers). If you pair Salesforce with Instantly, note that Instantly's native Salesforce integration retires on December 10, 2026; Instantly documents OutboundSync or Zapier as replacements.

Also worth a look: Zoho CRM Professional (25 × $23 billed annually, about $575/mo) is the lowest-cost credible option we found at this size.

### Spreadsheet or CRM?

At this size the CRM is the system of record; a spreadsheet works only for side lists.

Signals that it is time for a CRM (our rules of thumb, not benchmarks):

- **A second person works the pipeline.** A cofounder, first seller, contractor SDR or agency. Shared sheets struggle with ownership, duplicates and overwritten notes.
- **More than about 20–30 live deals or conversations at once.** Or a follow-up has slipped more than once.
- **You copy sequencer replies into the sheet by hand.** More than about 30 minutes a week. Most CRMs here receive replies from Instantly, Smartlead or lemlist directly.
- **Email and LinkedIn reach the same people.** One record per person stops you double-touching prospects.
- **Investor or board pipeline reporting takes more than about an hour a month.** Stage history and pipeline reports are built into every CRM listed, including free plans (depth varies).
- **Inbound leads arrive or your first sales hire starts.** Forms, routing and activity history make the handoff work.

Starter sheet columns: Company, Contact, Email, LinkedIn URL, Source, Stage, Next step, Next-step date, Deal value, Last touch, Notes. Every CRM listed imports a CSV, so nothing is lost when you switch. List prices as of 2026-11-10 from vendor pricing pages; verify with the vendor. Seat counts follow this page's assumptions. [All CRMs we list](https://profitableagentstack.com/use-cases/crm).

# Large / multi-team: AI GTM stack for 40+ GTM people, at least $7,587/mo

About at least $7,587/mo (list-price floor) for our recommended stack, estimated from published list prices as of 2026-11-02 to 2026-11-23 (per tool). Assumptions: 40+ GTM people across teams, 25 of them prospecting in Apollo (Organization, billed annually, 3-seat minimum), ~25 LinkedIn senders (HeyReach Agency tier), monthly list prices except Apollo and Common Room (billed annually, Common Room 5 seats). Clay is its Growth monthly list price; its Enterprise tier is custom. Salesloft (outbound) has no public price and counts as $0 here; expect a per-seat, annual quote with a seat minimum. Peec AI is Advanced's monthly list price; SSO needs its Enterprise quote. Enterprise tiers, SSO and security documents are quote-based. This total is a floor, not a quote. Actual cost depends on your usage, billing period, taxes and add-ons.

## Who this is for

More than forty people across several teams or regions. Procurement, security review and data-processing agreements are part of buying anything.

## Recommended stack (estimate)

One tool per job, no paid overlap. Each pick weighs two things: its value score and whether it fits a team of this size, judged from reviews by companies of similar size and from enterprise-readiness evidence. The value score is a category-wide number based on each tool's lowest published price (often a free plan), so a tool can be "best in category" and still not be the pick at this size. "Best in category" means the highest value score (ties included) among all tools we list for that use case.

- **Warm network & referrals.** Account-based; lives in the CRM.
- **ICP & positioning.** Owned by product marketing; no paid tool listed.

- **Investor or board pipeline reporting takes more than about an hour a month.** Stage history and pipeline reports are built into every CRM listed, including free plans (depth varies).
- **Inbound leads arrive or your first sales hire starts.** Forms, routing and activity history make the handoff work.

## What we found: who reviews these tools and enterprise readiness (as of 2026-11-05)

Security and plan statements come from each vendor's own pages and are vendor claims; reviewer company-size shares come from G2's public comparison pages (we do not show G2 star ratings we could not fetch). Everything may change; confirm security, SSO and compliance in writing before buying. This is not legal or compliance advice.

- **Apollo (list building).** Pricing page: Organization is $119 per seat per month billed annually with a 3-seat minimum, and SSO appears in its plan table (checked 2026-11-05). Trust center lists SOC 2, ISO/IEC 27001, GDPR and CCPA. Help center has an article on setting up SSO. Vendor enterprise page cites RBAC, permission profiles and audit logging; vendor customer story: Superside runs 130 reps on Apollo. These are vendor statements. [Source](https://www.apollo.io/pricing)
- **Apollo (G2 reviewer size).** G2 comparison page (checked 2026-11-05): of 9,858 Apollo reviews, 67.0% small-business (50 or fewer employees), 28.4% mid-market (51-1,000) and 4.6% enterprise (over 1,000). That is roughly 2,800 mid-market and 450 enterprise reviewers (our arithmetic from G2's percentages). [Source](https://www.g2.com/compare/apollo-io-vs-clay-com-clay)
- **ZoomInfo (not in our stack: contact sales).** G2 reviewers (8,728 reviews, checked 2026-11-05) are 25.8% small-business, 48.1% mid-market and 26.1% enterprise, the most enterprise-heavy list-building voice we found. It publishes no price (priced by licenses and credits). Vendor security materials state SOC 2 Type II and ISO certifications. Request a quote next to Apollo's. [Source](https://www.g2.com/compare/clay-com-clay-vs-zoominfo-sales)
- **Clay (enrichment).** Vendor pricing page (checked 2026-11-05): states SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, GDPR and CCPA. Enterprise (custom pricing, annual commitment) adds SSO/SAML, SCIM, RBAC, user groups with credit budgets, IP allowlists, and a custom CSA and DPA; Launch and Growth do not include SSO or RBAC. Named customer case studies on the page include Intercom, Verkada, Rippling and Hex. Growth is $495/mo monthly list ($446 annual view). G2: 234 reviews, 73.8% small-business, 24.8% mid-market, 1.4% enterprise; Hunter (659 reviews) shows 31.9% mid-market. [Source](https://www.clay.com/pricing)
- **Salesloft (outbound, our Large pick).** G2 comparison page (checked 2026-11-05): 4,287 reviews, 16.5% small-business, 50.9% mid-market, 32.6% enterprise; G2 ease of setup 8.6 vs Outreach 7.7, quality of support 8.6 vs 8.3. Vendor security page lists SOC 2 Type 2 and ISO 27001; its security measures document also lists ISO 27701; help center documents SAML SSO (Okta, OneLogin, Google, Microsoft Entra). Trust center is public. Pricing page goes to a talk-to-sales form (no list price). Vendor says Salesloft is now the company and platform brand after merging with Clari. [Source](https://www.g2.com/compare/outreach-vs-salesloft)
- **Salesloft (security and SSO).** Security & compliance page and help center (checked 2026-11-05). [Source](https://www.salesloft.com/security-compliance)
- **Outreach (outbound, also consider).** G2 comparison page (checked 2026-11-05): 3,574 reviews, 19.1% small-business, 59.2% mid-market, 21.7% enterprise; reviewers flag cost and a steeper learning curve more often. Vendor trust page lists SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, ISO 27701, ISO 42001 and HIPAA, but trust center access is through an account exec. Pricing page lists Amplify Essentials, Core, Plus and Pro with 10,000 to 100,000 AI credits and says pricing is per user plus consumption; no list price. [Source](https://www.outreach.io/pricing)
- **Reply.io and HeyReach spot-check.** Reply.io, our previous Large outbound pick, is 80.5% small-business, 17.4% mid-market, 2.1% enterprise (1,568 G2 reviews), so it moved to the all-tools list as a cheaper option. HeyReach (LinkedIn) has only 74 G2 reviews, so the LinkedIn pick is unchanged and no listed LinkedIn tool has a large enterprise review base. [Source](https://www.g2.com/compare/outreach-vs-salesloft)
- **Common Room.** Vendor security page lists a SOC 2 Type 2 report, GDPR and CCPA compliance, SSO/SAML/SCIM and role-based access control. [Source](https://www.commonroom.io/security/)
- **Reply.io.** Help center documents organization, multi-team and single-team roles and permissions; vendor white-label page says the platform is SOC 2 certified. [Source](https://support.reply.io/hc/reply-help-center/articles/roles-permissions-tab)
- **HeyReach.** Help center documents Admin and Member roles with per-feature permissions. Its data processing addendum says SSO (including SAML) is not currently supported, and we found no SOC 2 claim. [Source](https://help.heyreach.io/en/articles/11782284-how-to-invite-team-members-and-manage-role-based-permissions-in-heyreach)
- **Hunter.** Help center: unlimited team members at no extra cost on one shared credit pool, with Owner, Admin and Member roles. Vendor says a DPA is included and SOC 2 is for enterprise. [Source](https://help.hunter.io/en/articles/15654553-hunter-account-faqs)
- **Instantly.** Public sources we found disagree on whether a SOC 2 Type II report is held. Ask the vendor for its current report under NDA before buying. [Source](https://instantly.ai/dpa)
- **Peec AI (AEO pick) and Profound.** Peec pricing page (checked 2026-11-05): Starter $95, Pro $245, Advanced $495 per month; SOC 2 on every plan; SSO only on Enterprise (custom). Profound pricing page: Enterprise custom with SOC 2 and SSO/SAML; self-serve brand plans are not published. Vendor claims; we did not collect G2 reviewer-size data for AEO tools. [Source](https://peec.ai/pricing)

## Quick answers

# Quick answers about AI GTM tools and stacks

Short answers built from our data: the recommended stack and monthly cost for each GTM team size, the lowest published entry price in each of 16 use cases, and the CRM to pick. Every answer uses vendor list prices (last verified 2026-11-23) and links to the page with the math. Not advice; verify with vendors.

## Best AI GTM stack by team size

### What is the best AI GTM stack for a solo founder?

Our recommended stack is about $41/mo + €19 Waalaxy at list prices (last verified 2026-11-02 to 2026-11-23 (per tool)): List building & lead data: Apollo (Free Starter plan); Enrichment & verification: Hunter (Free plan (50 credits)); Outbound email / sequencing: Smartlead (Base, 1 workspace); LinkedIn outreach: Waalaxy (1 user × €19 (EUR, not converted)); Landing pages & websites: Carrd (Pro Standard, $19/yr ÷ 12); Newsletters: beehiiv (Free plan); Web analytics: Google Analytics (Free). CRM is separate and not in the total. Details: https://profitableagentstack.com/stages/solo-founder

### What is the best AI GTM stack for a 3-person GTM team?

A 3-person GTM team falls in our Small GTM team band (2–5 GTM people). Our recommended stack is about $106/mo + €38 Waalaxy (2 users) at list prices (last verified 2026-11-02 to 2026-11-23 (per tool)): List building & lead data: Apollo (Free Starter plan); Enrichment & verification: Hunter (Starter); Outbound email / sequencing: Instantly (Outreach Growth); LinkedIn outreach: Waalaxy (2 users × €19 (EUR, not converted)); Search performance: Google Search Console (Free); Social scheduling: Buffer (Free (up to 3 channels)); Landing pages & websites: Framer (Basic (yearly-billing view)); Newsletters: beehiiv (Free plan); Web analytics: Google Analytics (Free); Signals, intent & analytics: RB2B (Free plan). CRM is separate and not in the total. Details: https://profitableagentstack.com/stages/small-gtm-team

### What is the best AI GTM stack for a 10-person GTM team?

A 10-person GTM team falls in our Early scaling band (6–15 GTM people). Our recommended stack is about $913/mo at list prices (last verified 2026-11-02 to 2026-11-23 (per tool)): List building & lead data: Apollo (Free Starter plan); Enrichment & verification: Hunter (Growth); Outbound email / sequencing: Instantly (Outreach Hypergrowth (125,000 emails/mo)); LinkedIn outreach: HeyReach (Growth $79 × 5 senders); Signals, intent & analytics: RB2B (Starter); Search performance: Google Search Console (Free); Content optimization: Surfer (Discovery, billed yearly); AEO (AI search visibility): Peec AI (Starter, monthly); Social scheduling: Postiz (Team); Landing pages & websites: Framer (Basic (yearly-billing view)); Newsletters: beehiiv (Free plan); Web analytics: Google Analytics (Free); Product & funnel analytics: PostHog (Free allowance). CRM is separate and not in the total. Details: https://profitableagentstack.com/stages/early-scaling

### What is the best AI GTM stack for a 25-person GTM team?

A 25-person GTM team falls in our Scaling band (16–40 GTM people). ## Scoring

### How does Profitable Agent Stack score tools?

value\_score (0-100) = round(0.625 x fit + 0.375 x cost\_score). fit = editorial fit\_score (1-5) x 20. cost\_score = 100 - 60 x (entry\_price - lowest entry price in the use case) / (highest - lowest); contact-sales tools get no cost or value score. The published formula reserves 20% for user sentiment, but no sentiment or user-review data is used in any score today, so fit and cost are reweighted 62.5/37.5. Stack picks also weigh fit for the GTM team size (reviewer company-size mix, case studies, enterprise-readiness evidence). Full method: https://profitableagentstack.com/methodology


## Guides (articles)

[Articles](https://profitableagentstack.com/articles/) › When to add AEO (AI search visibility) vs classic SEO

# When to add AEO (AI search visibility) vs classic SEO

by [Limor Sinay](https://profitableagentstack.com/advisory), Profitable Agent Stack | [Artificial Intelligence (AI)](https://profitableagentstack.com/articles/category/ai), [Blog Posts](https://profitableagentstack.com/articles/category/blog-posts)

AEO tools track whether ChatGPT, Perplexity and Google's AI answers mention your brand. Classic search tools come first; add AEO when AI assistants already send you visits.

AEO (answer engine optimization, also called GEO) tools run a set of buyer questions through AI assistants and report whether your brand is mentioned or cited. Classic SEO tools tell you how you rank in search results. They are different jobs, so we list them as separate use cases: **Search performance**, **Content optimization** and **AEO (AI search visibility)**.

## A simple order

1. **Search performance first.** Google Search Console is free and shows which queries bring visitors. Most AI answers still draw on pages that rank, so this data helps both.
2. **Content optimization when you publish weekly.** A tool like Surfer helps each page match what searchers want. Before you publish regularly, it is a bill.
3. **AEO when AI search is a channel.** Add a tracker once AI assistants already send you visits you can see in your analytics, or your buyers say they ask ChatGPT first.

## What it costs

On the [published prices](https://profitableagentstack.com/directory) we checked: Peec AI starts at $95/mo for 50 prompts on 3 models, Otterly.AI at $29/mo for 15 prompts, and AthenaHQ and Scrunch at $295 and $250/mo. Profound is contact sales. Compare that with the $41/mo for a whole solo stack.

## What we recommend by size

- **Solo founder and small team:** skip. Warm leads and outbound produce more pipeline, and you have too little AI-search traffic to measure.
- **Early scaling and up:** one dedicated tracker. See the [early scaling stack](https://profitableagentstack.com/stages/early-scaling).
- **Large teams:** check SSO and security terms; several vendors reserve SSO for an enterprise quote.

## A caution

These tools measure answers that change from run to run, and none can guarantee a mention. Treat the numbers as a trend, not a score.

General information only, not advice. Prices as of 2026-11-23; verify with the vendor.

Published Nov 11, 2026


[Articles](https://profitableagentstack.com/articles/) › Why we size stacks by GTM team size, not funding stage

# Why we size stacks by GTM team size, not funding stage

by [Limor Sinay](https://profitableagentstack.com/advisory), Profitable Agent Stack | [Artificial Intelligence (AI)](https://profitableagentstack.com/articles/category/ai), [Blog Posts](https://profitableagentstack.com/articles/category/blog-posts)

Funding rounds say little about what tools you need. How many people do go-to-market says a lot.

Two companies can raise the same round and have very different go-to-market teams: one founder selling alone, the other with fifteen people. They need different tools and should pay different amounts.

## The five sizes

- **Solo founder:** 1 GTM person
- **Small GTM team:** 2–5
- **Early scaling:** 6–15
- **Scaling:** 16–40
- **Large / multi-team:** 40+

## What changes as the team grows

- **Cost shifts from tools to seats.** Per-sender and per-seat pricing starts to dominate around the point where several people run LinkedIn outreach.
- **Admin matters.** At some size you need roles, permissions and a way to offboard people.
- **Signals earn their place later than you think.** See [when to skip intent data](https://profitableagentstack.com/articles/when-to-skip-intent-data).
- **Procurement shows up.** Large teams need security documents and sometimes a sales call, and we say so when a tool is contact-sales.

## How we pick tools for each size

A tool's value score is category-wide and leans on its lowest published price, so a free plan can make a tool look like the best value for every team. For each size we also check who reviews and uses the tool: G2's reviewer company-size shares (50 or fewer employees, 51-1,000, over 1,000), customer stories that name team size, and for large teams security and admin evidence such as SSO, roles and SOC 2. That is why the 40+ stack counts a paid Apollo plan and picks Clay for enrichment, while solo and small stacks stay cost-first. Details are on the [methodology page](https://profitableagentstack.com/methodology).

## Where to start

Pick your size on the [stacks hub](https://profitableagentstack.com/stages/). Each page lists who it is for, the recommended stack with an estimated monthly cost, the use cases that matter at that size, the ones to skip, and the best-value tool for each job we include.

Sizes are planning bands, not rules. Estimates are not advice; verify prices with vendors.

Published Nov 9, 2026


[Articles](https://profitableagentstack.com/articles/) › When to skip intent data (and what to do first)

# When to skip intent data (and what to do first)

by [Limor Sinay](https://profitableagentstack.com/advisory), Profitable Agent Stack | [Artificial Intelligence (AI)](https://profitableagentstack.com/articles/category/ai), [Blog Posts](https://profitableagentstack.com/articles/category/blog-posts)

Intent and signals tools help you prioritize. If you have nobody worth prioritizing yet, they are an expensive distraction.

Intent and signals tools answer one question: *who should I contact first?* That is a great question once you have a list, a message and a sequence that sometimes gets replies. Before that, it is a bill.

## A simple test

Skip paid intent data until **all three** are true:

1. Your hand-built outbound already books meetings. Not once, repeatedly.
2. You have more good-fit accounts than you can contact this month.
3. A better order of contact would change what you do on Monday.

If any of these is false, spend the time on your message and your list instead.

## What it costs to be early

On the [published prices](https://profitableagentstack.com/directory) we checked: RB2B has a free plan and a Starter plan at $79/mo, while Common Room's Essential plan is $2,500/mo billed annually for 5 seats. A solo founder's whole recommended stack costs about $41/mo. Paying for intent data first can cost more than the rest of the stack combined.

## What to use instead

- **Solo founder:** skip signals entirely. Message your warm network and send simple outbound. See the [solo founder stack](https://profitableagentstack.com/stages/solo-founder).
- **Small GTM team:** the free RB2B plan is enough, and only once meetings are already coming in.
- **Early scaling:** a low-cost visitor-identification tool starts to earn its place.
- **Scaling and above:** signals belong in the core stack. Pay for them when a real prioritization problem exists.

## One more caution

Visitor identification and intent data raise privacy and consent questions that depend on where your buyers live. Check your obligations before you switch anything on.

General information only, not legal or financial advice. Prices as of 2026-11-23; verify with the vendor.

Published Nov 6, 2026


[Articles](https://profitableagentstack.com/articles/) › One tool per job: how to stop paying twice

# One tool per job: how to stop paying twice

by [Limor Sinay](https://profitableagentstack.com/advisory), Profitable Agent Stack | [Artificial Intelligence (AI)](https://profitableagentstack.com/articles/category/ai), [Blog Posts](https://profitableagentstack.com/articles/category/blog-posts)

Most GTM stacks pay for the same job two or three times. Here is how we pick one tool per job and explain each pick.

Tool sprawl is quiet. A sequencer here, a second enrichment plan there, and a scheduler nobody opened since March. Each is small; together they are a real line on the budget.

## The rule

For every use case, pick **one** tool, write down why, and revisit it monthly. Our recommended stacks follow that rule with no paid overlap, and each row on a stack page says why that tool won.

## How to choose

1. **Name the job narrowly.** "Outbound email sequencing" is a job. "Sales automation" is not.
2. **Start from the free tier.** Several jobs are covered at $0 (for example Google Search Console for search data, or a free newsletter plan). Prove you need more before paying.
3. **Compare on value, not features.** We rank tools in each use case by [value score](https://profitableagentstack.com/articles/how-we-score), then explain any pick that is not the top score.
4. **Count seats honestly.** Per-sender or per-seat pricing, such as LinkedIn tools, is where costs grow fastest as the team grows.

## When two tools in one stack is fine

Two tools are fine when they do **different** jobs. In our stacks, Search Console tracks search performance while Surfer optimizes content, and RB2B identifies site visitors while PostHog analyzes product usage. That is two jobs, not one job paid for twice.

## See it in practice

The [stacks by GTM team size](https://profitableagentstack.com/stages/) show one pick per job at each size, with the monthly estimate and the use cases we would skip.

General information only. Prices change; verify with vendors. Prices as of 2026-11-23.

Published Nov 4, 2026


[Articles](https://profitableagentstack.com/articles/) › How we score AI GTM tools (and why cost counts)

# How we score AI GTM tools (and why cost counts)

by [Limor Sinay](https://profitableagentstack.com/advisory), Profitable Agent Stack | [Artificial Intelligence (AI)](https://profitableagentstack.com/articles/category/ai), [Blog Posts](https://profitableagentstack.com/articles/category/blog-posts)

The value score in plain words: what goes in, what does not, and why money never changes rank.

Every tool in the [directory](https://profitableagentstack.com/directory) gets one number: a **value score** from 0 to 100. Here is exactly what is behind it, so you can disagree with it intelligently.

## What goes in

- **Fit (50%).** An editorial 1–5 judgment of how well the tool does its one job, converted to 0–100. It is an opinion, and we say so.
- **Cost (30%).** Inside each use case, the lowest published starting price scores 100 and the highest scores 40, scaled in between. A tool with no public price gets no cost score and therefore no value score.
- **Sentiment (20%).** Reserved for public G2 or Capterra ratings, used only when we can fetch them with a source and a date. Right now we cannot, so fit and cost carry the score (62.5% and 37.5%).

## What stays out

- **Affiliate links and sponsorships.** Payment never changes a score, a badge or an order. See the [affiliate disclosure](https://profitableagentstack.com/disclosure).
- **Prices we could not verify.** Those are shown as "price not yet verified" instead of guessed.

## Where the cost estimates come from

Each stack on the [stacks-by-GTM-size hub](https://profitableagentstack.com/stages/) adds up published monthly list prices for the stated tiers and seats, with the math shown. They are estimates: they exclude taxes, add-ons, overages and annual discounts, and prices change. Always verify with the vendor.

## Scores do not pick the stack alone

The score ranks tools within one use case. For a stack at a given team size we also weigh who reviews the tool at that size and, for large teams, enterprise readiness such as SSO and security documents. When the two disagree, for example a free plan that tops the score but is not what a 40-person team would run, we follow the size evidence and explain why on the stack page.

## The honest limits

A score cannot know your market, your data or your team. Use it to shortlist, then run a trial. The full method lives on the [methodology page](https://profitableagentstack.com/methodology), and if you spot an error, the [corrections page](https://profitableagentstack.com/corrections) is the fastest way to tell us.

General information only, not professional, legal or financial advice. Prices as of 2026-11-23.

Published Nov 2, 2026


## Page: https://profitableagentstack.com/methodology

# How do you rank tools and choose stacks?

Value score (0–100) = 50% use-case fit + 30% cost + 20% user sentiment. Until sentiment data is verified, fit and cost are reweighted to 62.5% / 37.5%. Recommended stacks do not use the score alone: each pick also has to fit the GTM team size, based on reviews from companies of that size and enterprise-readiness evidence.

## How we choose a stack pick for a team size

Two checks, in this order. (a) Value score: it ranks tools inside one use case and is driven by the lowest published starting price, which is often a free plan, so it favors tools that are cheap to start. (b) Fit for that GTM team size: we look for who actually reviews and uses the tool, using G2 reviewer company-size shares (small business: 50 or fewer employees, mid-market: 51–1,000, enterprise: over 1,000), vendor case studies that name team size, and for large teams security and admin evidence (SSO, roles, SOC 2, data processing terms). If a high-scoring tool is mostly reviewed by small teams, or its free plan is not what a 40-person team would run, the stack uses a paid tier with a quote flag, or a different tool, and says why. Solo and small stacks stay cost-first because free and entry plans still match those sizes.

## What size-segmented evidence we show

On the Scaling and Large stack pages we list what we found, with the source link and the date checked. We show reviewer company-size shares from G2's public comparison pages and link to the filtered review pages. We do not show G2 star ratings, because we could not fetch them reliably, and we do not estimate them. Counts such as "roughly 2,800 mid-market reviewers" are our arithmetic from G2's percentages and are labeled that way. Reviewer mix is a signal, not proof: it shows who talks about a tool, not how well it works for your team.

## Limits

Some job categories have no listed tool with a large mid-market or enterprise review base (outbound and LinkedIn outreach, for example). We say so on the Large page rather than pretend otherwise. Contact-sales tools such as ZoomInfo get no value score because they have no public price, and may appear as an option to quote rather than in the priced stack.

## Fit score (editorial)

An editorial 1–5 judgment of how well the tool serves its use case, converted to 0–100 (×20). It is an opinion, not a measurement, and is reviewed when vendors or readers send corrections.

## Cost score

Within each use case, the lowest published starting price scores 100 and the highest scores 40, scaled linearly. Tools without a public price (contact sales or not yet verified) get no cost score and no value score.

## Sentiment score

Will use public G2 or Capterra ratings (rating ÷ 5 × 100) only when fetched with a source link and date. As of 2026-11-23 these sites blocked automated checks, so sentiment is not yet included and we link to reviews instead.

## CRM is shown separately

Each team-size page has its own CRM section with a pick, a runner-up and when a spreadsheet is enough. CRM costs are not added to stack totals, because many teams already have a CRM or start on a spreadsheet.

## Stack cost estimates

Sum of published monthly list prices for the stated tiers, seats and volumes on each GTM-team-size page. Labeled estimates; excludes taxes, add-ons and overages.

## Money never changes rank

Sponsorships and affiliate links do not change scores, prices or order.

# What changed this week?

Updated 2026-11-23. The latest AI GTM tool releases and price changes we have logged, newest first, each with a source link.

**2026-11-23** — New this week: Reply.io (listed) released Jason Harness (Nov 20), a free, open-source (MIT) AI SDR harness that runs inside Claude Code or Codex as nine roles (planner, researcher, copywriter, critic and more). Reply sends the emails and LinkedIn messages and a person approves every send. In alpha; uses your own AI subscription, Reply plans still paid. [Source](https://www.einpresswire.com/article/957995784/reply-io-launches-open-source-jason-harness-for-outbound-sales)

**2026-11-23** — New this week: Clay (listed) opened its global agent in beta (Nov 19): you describe a play in chat and it builds the search, audience, workflow and sequence, tests on sample records and shows an estimated cost before running at scale. Included on paid Launch, Growth and Enterprise plans. [Source](https://www.clay.com/blog/clay-global-agent-beta)

**2026-11-23** — New this week: Swan AI (listed) moved its automations into goal-based agents (Nov 17): each agent owns one goal, such as booking first meetings with accounts showing buying signals, reviews its own results every few days and asks before bigger changes like new outreach or more credits. Prices unchanged. [Source](https://www.getswan.com/changelog/agents)

**2026-11-23** — New this week: Spara announced Scout (Nov 17), a proactive sales assistant that watches job changes, company news, buying signals and CRM activity, then drafts outreach and next steps for reps to review in Slack or text. ## Page: https://profitableagentstack.com/review-policy

# How do you handle reviews and ratings?

We never fabricate, buy or edit reviews or ratings. We show only public ratings from G2 or Capterra with a source link and date checked, or a link to the reviews.

## Third-party ratings

Ratings belong to their sources and are shown as of the date checked. They may change. G2 and Capterra are trademarks of their owners and do not endorse us.

## Reader feedback

Feedback submitted through "Share your experience" (not live yet) may be moderated. We will not publish it as a rating, and we will remove content that is fake, abusive, defamatory or from someone with an undisclosed conflict of interest. Vendors may not review their own products.

## Incentives

We do not offer incentives for reviews. If that changes, incentivized feedback will be labeled.


## Page: https://profitableagentstack.com/disclosure

**Affiliate disclosure:** this page includes affiliate links (marked "affiliate"). If you buy through them, The Sinay Way LLC may earn a commission at no extra cost to you. It never changes scores, prices or order. See our [disclosure](https://profitableagentstack.com/disclosure).

# How do you make money?

We may earn affiliate commissions or accept labeled sponsorships, and The Sinay Way LLC offers advisory services. None of this changes prices, scores or rank.

Last updated 2026-11-23. This page is a general notice for a small site. It is not legal advice, and it has not been reviewed by a lawyer.

## Affiliate links

Some links may be affiliate links; if you buy through them, The Sinay Way LLC may earn a commission at no extra cost to you. Affiliate links are marked "affiliate" and tagged rel="sponsored"; pages that contain them carry a disclosure at the top. As of 2026-11-23 affiliate links are active for: Smartlead, Salesforge, lemlist, Woodpecker, FullEnrich, HeyReach, Waalaxy, RB2B, beehiiv, Kit, Descript.

## Sponsored placements

Any sponsored listing will be clearly labeled "Sponsored". None are sold at present.

## Our own services

This site is operated by The Sinay Way LLC as part of its advisory services, and we promote those services, including on some stack pages. They are provided only under a separate signed agreement; outcomes are not guaranteed. Recommended stacks are chosen by the published method, not to sell services.

## Scores and reviews

Payment never changes fit, cost or value scores, badges, or which third-party ratings are shown. We do not accept payment for reviews.

## FTC

This disclosure is intended to follow the U.S. FTC Guides Concerning the Use of Endorsements and Testimonials in Advertising.


## Page: https://profitableagentstack.com/about

# Who runs Profitable Agent Stack?

A cost-first directory of AI go-to-market tools operated by The Sinay Way LLC as part of its advisory services. We list published prices with source links and dates, and mark tools without public pricing as contact sales. We do not invent prices, features or reviews.


## Disclaimer
Profitable Agent Stack is for general information only, provided "as is" without warranties. Prices, plans, features and review data change often and may be inaccurate or out of date (last checked 2026-11-23); always verify with the vendor. Cost estimates and scores are editorial estimates, not advice. Nothing here is professional, legal or financial advice. Trademarks belong to their owners; listing is not endorsement. Some links may be affiliate or sponsored — see our Disclosure.
